rules.reason: Apps rebuild their cache files when they need them, so removing them frees space without losing your data. The first launch afterwards can be a little slower.
Log files are only needed to find out what went wrong. Look before you remove one that an app is still writing.
Crash reports are only useful if you are debugging that crash. Keep the ones you still need.
Homebrew keeps the files it downloaded. It downloads them again when it needs them. Close Terminal sessions that are running brew first.
npm keeps a download cache and repairs or refills it by itself. Close any npm command that is running first.
Cargo keeps the Rust packages it downloaded and fetches them again when a build needs them. Close any cargo build first.
Cargo unpacks downloaded Rust packages here and does it again when a build needs them. Close any cargo build first.
Cargo keeps copies of Git projects your Rust code depends on and clones them again when needed. Close any cargo build first.
Gradle keeps downloaded libraries and compiled build scripts and rebuilds them on the next build. The next build will be slower. Close Android Studio and any Gradle build first.
Xcode keeps build files here and rebuilds them, so the next build of that project is slower. Quit Xcode first.
Xcode copied debug files from your iPhone or iPad. It copies them again the next time you connect that device, which takes a few minutes. Quit Xcode first.
Yarn keeps the packages it downloaded and fetches them again when needed. Close any yarn command first.
pip keeps downloaded Python packages and fetches them again when needed. Close any pip command first.
